name: Conclave
summary: A Claude Code plugin, with its own single-plugin marketplace, that ships a software team as subagents and a lead that sizes each task before spending tokens. Maintained by one developer; installed into other projects from git, cached by version.

components.name: plugin
pitfalls: An unchanged version never reaches users: installs are cached by version, so every change under plugins/ bumps plugin.json and marketplace.json together.
Plugin agents ignore permissionMode, hooks and mcpServers in their frontmatter; write limits are prose in the body.
conventions: Agent bodies carry no project names, paths, commands or framework names; anything project-specific comes from .claude/conclave.json through the prompt or from a stack pack (docs/design.md, Agent file conventions).
Return shapes (SPEC, PLAN, DEV, CHALLENGE, FINDINGS, VERDICT, TESTS, DOCS, QA) are shared with the workflow scripts: change both or neither.

Adding a stack is a skills/stack-<name>/SKILL.md with the sections Idioms, Review checklist, Testing, Tooling, Pitfalls, the enum entry in schemas/conclave.schema.json and a README row; no agent or script changes.
Escalation is uniform: a workflow returns status needs-human with decision_request from any phase and the lead handles every one the same way.

components.name: workflows
pitfalls: Workflow scripts use top-level return, which node --check rejects; syntax-check a scratch copy with a stub line defining args, agent, parallel, pipeline, phase, log, budget, the body wrapped in async function main(){...} and export const meta replaced by const meta.
conventions: The script never decides tier, rounds, lenses or models; the lead does, in exec. Keep that split when adding a phase.
Return shapes are shared with the agents' What you return sections: change both or neither.
A workflow returns status needs-human with decision_request from any phase; never a phase-specific escalation shape.

components.name: hooks
conventions: A deny reason never contains the matched value.
Rule names are stable: CONCLAVE_ALLOW refers to them, so renaming one is a breaking change.
Subagents never commit or push; the hooks enforce it, the lead proposes a commit and waits.

components.name: bin
conventions: Gate scripts are generic: they take the project's paths and refs as arguments and read nothing project-specific from the environment.

stakes: ships a broken prompt, workflow or guardrail to every project that installs the plugin: a wrong guardrail blocks legitimate work or lets a secret or an unapproved commit through, and a wrong return shape stalls every pipeline run

security.threat_model: The hooks run with the user's own permissions on every tool call in every project that installs the plugin. A deny reason must never echo the matched secret, subagents must not be able to commit or push, and nothing shipped in plugins/ may carry personal data, local paths or project-specific values.
